Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 15:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Sofia Delgado (Redwood AE), Marcus Lee (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (CTO, Portfolio AI), Liam O'Connor (ML Eng), Joel Rivera (Infra), Sara Kim (Product)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to validate time-to-first-token (TTFT) expectations, free credits for pilot, and which hosting path (hosted vs dedicated vs private) Portfolio AI should pursue given latency, PII, and throughput constraints. Action items and next steps captured.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Sofia: hey everybody, thanks for joining. i'm sofia from Redwood, im the account owner. quick intro — marcus will cover the technical bits. nina, do you want to do a 30s context of what you're trying to build?
[00:18] Nina: yeah sure thanks. we're Portfolio AI, we build an assistant that summarizes investor decks and does Q&A over private client data. privacy is huge for us, but so is latency — traders need answers in sub-400ms for short prompts. we're evaluating whether to start with Redwood hosted for speed to market or go directly into Dedicated or Private.
[00:35] Marcus: got it. hi all. from the SE side i'll try to map constraints to latency/cost tradeoffs, and give a sense for ttft — how fast you can go from sign-up to first real call.
[00:49] Liam: couple things up front — we have PII in docs, some redaction already, but legal will probably require SOC 2 and KMS integration for keys. also we may want an on-prem option for certain clients later.
[01:08] Joel: network wise we run in GCP with a strict egress policy, so vpc peering or private endpoints needed, and we have fixed IPs we want to allowlist.
[01:22] Sofia: excellent, that's the exact set of concerns our customers ask about. quick framing: there are three paths — Redwood Hosted (fastest ttft, quick credits, low onboarding friction), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools, predictable latency at scale), Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem for strict compliance). for a pilot we usually recommend starting hosted with credits to validate prompts and metrics, then migrate if you need private networking or a committable SLA.
[01:45] Nina: curious — how fast is ttft with hosted in practice? like from account creation to first real request with auth and basic SSO?
[01:56] Marcus: in a PLG flow we routinely see devs hitting first token within an hour if they go self-serve and use our SDKs. realistic time if you need SOC2 review or an SSO config is more like 1-3 days because of security paperwork. for us to run a meaningful latency benchmark we recommend a small-batch test — we'll give you a script that uses quantized model variants and a few seq lengths to show p50/p95.
[02:24] Liam: okay that hour number is promising — but the p50/p95 numbers matter. you mentioned quantized variants — how does that affect answer quality?
[02:34] Marcus: good question. quantization reduces memory / cost and can slightly change outputs. our Optimize tooling suggests profiles based on your prompt distributions. for deck summarization shorter sequences are typical so you can often use int8 or 4-bit profiles without much degradation; we also recommend prefix caching for repeated doc chunks.
[02:53] Nina: notation / transcription is fine but legal will ask for encryption at rest with our KMS and audit logs. does Redwood Hosted support customer-managed keys?
[03:03] Sofia: hosted supports KMS integration for enterprise customers — that's usually a dedicated or private tier feature, but for pilots we can enable a KMS workflow under a dedicated agreement. we can send the security pack that details KMS, audit logs, SSO (SAML/Okta) and SOC2 status.
[03:19] Joel: and network — can hosted do private endpoints? or do we need Redwood Private for VPC peering?
[03:26] Marcus: hosted has private endpoint options in certain regions and for enterprise accounts, but full VPC peering and on-prem is only in Redwood Private. Dedicated can give you reserved capacity with IP allowlisting and private infra within a cloud account but not full customer-controlled VPC like Private.
[03:44] Sara: from a product timeline perspective, we want a pilot within two weeks to test throughput on sample decks. how much free credit do you usually provide?
[03:54] Sofia: for early pilots we typically do a small credit allocation that covers approx 10k-50k tokens depending on deliverables; for more involved benchmarks or multi-team pilots we can extend that. i'll propose a credits plan in the follow-up.
[04:08] Nina: is that enough to run the benchmark Marcus suggested? we need a test that simulates 50 requests per second for 1 minute at varying seq lengths.
[04:17] Marcus: the small script can be run against a quantized model variant — it won't exactly emulate full sustained load but it'll give p50/p95 for cold vs warmed k v cache. for 50 rps sustained you'd want Dedicated or a burst policy on hosted; for the pilot we can simulate and extrapolate.
[04:36] Liam: you mentioned KV cache — if we do a conversational flow with a lot of context, is the cache per-tenant or per-model instance? some vendors mix caching and it causes cross-tenant leakage concerns.
[04:48] Marcus: it's per-tenant. we log caching metrics and traces in Console so you can see hit rates. we also offer prefix-only caching mode if you want to be extra conservative.
[04:59] Nina: what about cost math — if we start hosted and later lift to Dedicated, how predictable are the unit costs? we want to avoid surprises.
[05:09] Sofia: Hosted is usage-based and can fluctuate; Dedicated gives you predictable throughput cost via reserved capacity. we provide a migration plan: you can pin model versions and rollout policies, and we can estimate break-even point given your qps and avg tokens per request. i'll include a cost comparison spreadsheet.
[05:28] Joel: legal will want to see an SLA for downtime and latency if we commit to dedicated. is that standard?
[05:35] Sofia: yes Dedicated comes with an SLA and optional premium support. Private has the strictest controls and can be packaged with an enterprise contract.
[05:42] Sara: any limitations on model catalog in Private vs Hosted? we have some fine-tuned models we want to bring.
[05:49] Marcus: you can bring your fine-tuned models to Dedicated and Private; hosted has a curated catalog but we also onboard customer models under enterprise/private agreements. there can be some kernel compatibility steps for certain architectures but we handle model onboarding as part of the Dedicated/Private plan.
[06:06] Nina: around SSO — our security team uses Okta and scoping SAML config usually takes a week. will that block the pilot?
[06:13] Sofia: not necessarily — you can start with API keys or short-lived tokens for the pilot; SAML/SSO can be done in parallel.
[06:21] Joel: about data residency — some of our clients insist EU-only. does Redwood host in EU regions?
[06:26] Marcus: yes we run in multiple cloud regions and can route requests by region; Private can be fully air-gapped for on-prem needs.
[06:33] (brief cross-talk)
[06:37] Nina: can you share the security pack now? even a one-pager is fine.
[06:41] Sofia: yes i'll send link to security-pack and SOC2 summary after the call — link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack (placeholder).
[06:50] Liam: one more technical — for extraction we use long documents and chunking, will Redwood recommend batching or continuous streaming?
[06:57] Marcus: for long doc extraction we recommend prefix/KV caching plus chunked streaming; continuous batching helps throughput but can add a small latency tail. tradeoff depends on your SLAs.
[07:11] Sara: ok timeline — we want pilot in two weeks and then a decision on hosting by end of month. how do you normally structure pilot success criteria?
[07:20] Sofia: standard pilot success metrics: p50/p95 latency targets, cost per 1k tokens, and accuracy on a small eval prompt set (we can help design). we'll do a kickoff, runbook, and a 4-week POC with checkpoints.
[07:33] Nina: for accuracy checks can Redwood run evals on our seeded prompts without keeping docs? privacy wise we need assurance data won't be retained.
[07:41] Marcus: for pilots we support ephemeral logging — we can disable telemetry retention and ensure logs are scoped. we'll note that in the security doc.
[07:50] (brief pause)
[07:54] Joel: about metrics — will we get token-level breakdown and model-level dashboards?
[07:58] Sofia: yes Console has token-level cost, latency breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and tracing hooks. we'll include screenshots in the follow-up.
[08:08] Liam: any gotchas you see with our stack? GCP, strict egress, okta, long docs.
[08:14] Marcus: the main gating factors are VPC/private endpoint for legal and KMS if you need CMK; otherwise it's mostly integration time. for throughput you'll need to decide if hosted bursts suffice or whether reserved capacity makes sense.
[08:28] Nina: ok let's summarize next steps.
[08:30] Sofia: recap: we'll send security pack + SOC2 summary, cost comparison spreadsheet, pilot credits proposal, and Marcus will send the benchmark script. Joel will share network diagram. we'll schedule a follow-up technical runbook next week.
[08:44] Nina: sounds good. thanks all.
[08:46] Sofia: thanks everyone.
[08:49] (call ends)

References shared in call: security-pack link, benchmark script (to be attached), cost spreadsheet (to be attached).
